answer: Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. Fingerprints are counted in umber, thus the distribution is public, and zenith lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a hollow header, so 3891 keys running one model collapse to a single share. A farm of 235 pays that 39 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
